input: Find a flatmate to split rent costs

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user has a place already or is searching for one together with a flatmate completely changes the starting point and steps of the plan.
The type of flatmate they are open to (friend, stranger, specific gender, age range, professional) shapes where and how to search.
The city, neighbourhood, or specific property location determines which platforms, communities, and networks are most relevant.
A hard move-in deadline creates urgency and dictates how aggressive or broad the search needs to be.
Knowing which channels they have already tried avoids redundant suggestions and focuses the plan on untapped options.
Lifestyle compatibility priorities (e.g. quiet vs social, pet-friendly, work-from-home) determine the vetting criteria and how to write a flatmate listing.
Understanding what a successful outcome looks like — a signed agreement, a trial period, or just a shortlist of candidates — defines when the task is done.

gold.taskTitle: Find a flatmate to split rent costs
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find a suitable person to share their living space with in order to divide rental expenses.

questions.title: Do you already have a flat, or are you searching together?
questions.description: Establishes whether the user has an existing property to fill a room in, or needs to find a place jointly with a future flatmate.

questions.title: What type of person are you open to living with?
questions.description: Clarifies preferences around gender, age, profession, or whether they want a friend vs a stranger as a flatmate.

questions.title: Which city or neighbourhood is the flat located in?
questions.description: Identifies the location so the plan can point to the most relevant local platforms, Facebook groups, or community boards.

questions.title: When do you need a flatmate to move in by?
questions.description: Determines urgency and whether the search needs to be broad and fast, or can be selective over a longer period.

questions.title: Which search methods have you already tried?
questions.description: Avoids recommending channels the user has already exhausted and focuses the plan on new, untested avenues.

questions.title: What lifestyle habits matter most to you in a flatmate?
questions.description: Uncovers non-negotiable compatibility factors such as noise levels, guests, cleanliness, pets, or remote working habits.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Defines the finish line — whether it is a signed tenancy agreement, a vetted shortlist, or simply a confirmed trial period with a candidate.
